paper.title: Asking Before Acting: Gather Information in Embodied Decision Making with Language Models
paper.central_claim: Asking Before Acting (ABA) lets an LLM agent proactively query external information sources in natural language while acting in embodied environments, improving performance and efficiency over baseline LLM agents across text-based household, robot-arm and real-world open-domain tasks; ABA-FT (finetuning on reformulated question metadata) gives further gains, especially on tasks baselines struggle with.
paper.scope_decision: in_scope (borderline): frozen/finetuned LLM agents (Vicuna-7B, GPT-3.5, GPT-4) with an ask action, evaluated closed loop in ALFWorld (text household with aligned embodied worlds) and on a simulated Ravens UR5e arm; the informant and the Ravens captioner read simulator ground truth (privileged); the real-world part is human-executed and is not counted as embodied evidence.

preliminary_judgment: Written after reading the fixed text, before opening this paper's seat records: system_method (+ ABA-FT component training); ALFWorld ID/OOD success over 5 (Vicuna) / 3 (GPT-3.5) seeds with sd, same backbone/K/scoring as ReAct; the informant (Vicuna-7B) reads ground-truth placements (72.5% on 40 questions) and ReAct gets no equivalent channel, so the gain bundles information access with asking; Ambiguous/Multiround figure-only; Ravens 20 trials/setting with captions from simulator coordinates; real world human-executed, no counts. Expected online, scoped; causality and holdout limited by the privileged channel; original-card fit doubtful (no sound solver).

signatures.object: an ask action added to an LLM agent's action space (think/ask/act) in ALFWorld and Ravens robot-arm tasks
signatures.information: text observations (ALFWorld) or oracle captions with ground-truth coordinates (robot arm); instruction; K=2 (ALFWorld) or K=1 manually written in-context trajectories with metadata/ask steps; answers from H (LLM given simulator ground-truth object placement)
signatures.operation: LLM emits a rationale ('metadata') then a natural-language question; H answers; the answer is appended to the history and used to choose the next action
signatures.output: environment actions (go to / take / move_to coordinates) after one or more asks
signatures.conditions: an answerer exists, is cheap and mostly right (72.5% on a 40-question check); ambiguity or hidden object locations are present
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: none; the model decides when to ask via in-context examples (Multiround adds an explicit self-query 'have I seen X' step)
signatures.persistence: history within the episode; Multiround keeps knowledge across tasks inside one room
signatures.later_use: agent re-reads earlier answers/observations through the self-query when a later task needs the object
signatures.claimed_effect: higher success and shorter trajectories than ReAct with the same backbone
signatures.failure_boundary: H errors or uninformative answers stall the agent; agent can wrongly conclude an object is unusable

signatures.object: ABA-FT: Vicuna-7B LoRA finetuned on D_QA (ask-or-not QA about 'have you seen X') and D_pi (policy with corrupted actions masked)
signatures.information: expert (privileged) PDDL trajectories and simulator ground truth produce templated questions and CoT; student sees only its own observations and the answers
signatures.operation: teacher-forced SFT of one LLM for all tasks of an environment variant
signatures.output: a student that asks and acts without ICL examples
signatures.conditions: expert policy can be written from PDDL/ground truth; 1500 (Ambiguous) / 500 (Multiround) trajectories
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: noise injected with p=0.2 and masked out of the policy loss
signatures.later_use: used in the Ambiguous / Multiround evaluation
signatures.claimed_effect: ABA-FT > ABA, especially in long-horizon Multiround

gap.author_gap: Frontier-model agents deployed in unfamiliar environments or with vague instructions explore inefficiently and fail; humans ask peers instead.
gap.checked_gap: ReAct's qualitative failure (loops, hallucinated finds) and its collapse as the number of required answers grows (robot arm 95% -> 5%) support an information-gathering problem in this setting; but the baseline never receives the oracle information ABA is allowed to ask for.
lineage: ReAct / SayCan / Inner Monologue (LLM agents with think/act, scene feedback) -> ABA (open-domain natural-language querying as an action, metadata ICL, FT)
NAV/IL ask-for-oracle-action work (Nguyen & Daume, Singh et al.) = what ABA replaces with free-form language

gap.residue: How much of the gain comes from learning when/what to ask (the metadata mechanism) versus simply having an oracle channel is not separated; a prompt-given-all-information or exhaustive-exploration control is absent.
gap.stakes: Efficiency and success of embodied LLM agents when instructions are ambiguous or the environment is unknown.
gap.method_response: Treat asking as a first-class action, teach its rationale via metadata examples or finetuning, and answer with an external information source.
gap.remaining_gap: Reliability of the answerer (72.5%), real robot execution (human/perfect controller), over-asking cost, and uncertainty about when to stop asking (authors + ours).
gap.unresolved: Neighbour papers are not pinned; 'pioneers' priority claim cannot be checked from the materials.
gap.aggregate_note: son55 gap retained: the residual (asking policy vs oracle information) is not separated because no information-matched baseline exists.

rs_pattern.reason: Resolved toward son55. The operation adds a natural-language ask action to an LLM agent, backed by an external information source (an LLM given simulator ground truth), and teaches when to ask through rationale-augmented examples or SFT. decompose_and_delegate/C25 needs a sound external solver or mechanically checkable oracle, typed machine-checkable handoffs and closure through verifiable output, and its success condition excludes privileged external supervision. Here the "solver" is a 72.5%-accurate LLM playing a human, the handoff is free-form prose, and the answers are privileged facts rather than solver output; sol's own checks mark these partial or failing. assumption_audit_and_pivot (guarantees/defences; proof/security sub-cards), reframe_as_solvable_object (no solver imported from the Contextual-MDP restatement) and adapt_via_conditioning/C03 (no conditioning substrate or category holdout) also do not fit. outside_taxonomy is recorded without forcing a label, and the paper is fully evaluated.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop, simulator-judged success in ALFWorld and the Ravens UR5e simulator. Not transfer: the Ravens perception and the informant are privileged (EVIDENCE rule 3, anchor precedent 1), examples are hand-made per environment (rule 2), and the real-world part has no robot and no trial counts (rule 1).
assessment.author_claim_preserved: ABA lets an LLM agent proactively query external sources in natural language while acting, giving substantial advantages in performance and efficiency over baseline LLM agents in text-based household, robot-arm and real-world open-domain embodied tasks; ABA-FT gives further gains, especially where baselines struggle.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In ALFWorld and a Ravens block-placement simulator, an LLM agent given an ask action and an LLM informant that holds the ground-truth object layout beats a no-ask ReAct with the same backbone and examples on success and trajectory length; the gain cannot be attributed to the metadata/learning mechanism and does not extend to real robots.

G.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Concrete gap: LLM agents with underspecified instructions or unknown object locations explore inefficiently, and ReAct's failure profile (loops, hallucinated finds, 95%->5% as required answers grow) is observable. Not 4: the nearest language-asking neighbours (Inner Monologue's human scene/preference queries, uncertainty-triggered asking) are named but not run, and the "pioneers" framing overreaches.

M.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Asking as a first-class action, rationale metadata in examples and QA-reformulated finetuning are tied to the gap and predict fewer physical actions and ask-before-explore behaviour. Key assumption weak: the answerer is reliable (72.5% on 40 questions) and holds ground-truth placements. The metadata rationale is never contrasted with plain asking.

X.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Interaction format, informant prompt, ABA-FT data recipe (rule-based PDDL/GT expert, noise p=0.2 masked, LoRA r=16, steps, 1500/500 trajectories) and the Ravens setup are given in appendices.
